title: Open Profiling Dataset — Offender Profile
description: Schema for a single offender profile. Every substantive claim is a Claim object carrying its own sources and confidence level. Unsourced assertions are structurally impossible.

tier.description: 1 = primary record (court filings, trial transcripts, official investigative reports, government statistics). 2 = peer-reviewed academic literature. 3 = book-length journalism with a sourcing apparatus. 4 = contemporaneous news reporting. See docs/sourcing-policy.md. Dramatisations, unsourced podcasts, wikis and AI-generated text are NOT admissible at any tier.

citation.description: Full citation. For court records use the reporter citation, e.g. 'Bundy v. State, 471 So. 2d 9 (Fla. 1985)'. For books include author, title, publisher, year and page.

value.description: The asserted value. MUST be null when confidence is 'unverified'.

confidence.description: established = corroborated by two or more independent sources, at least one tier 1 or 2. reported = a single credible source. contested = credible sources disagree; record the disagreement in 'notes'. unverified = no admissible source found; value must be null.

sources.description: MUST be non-empty unless confidence is 'unverified'. Enforced by scripts/validate.py.

notes.description: Required when confidence is 'contested' or 'unverified': state what the disagreement is, or what was searched and not found.

id.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country of principal offences, sequence number, surname. e.g. USA-001-BUNDY

record_status.description: 'complete' requires that every field in the completeness checklist is either populated or explicitly marked unverified with a note.

ai_assisted.description: Set true if any part of this record was drafted with a language model. Required disclosure. AI-drafted text is never itself a source; every claim must still carry an admissible human-verifiable citation.

media_epithet.description: Press nickname. Recorded as a media artefact, not as a descriptor endorsed by this dataset.

judicial_status.description: Current legal status. Convictions only. A person not convicted of an offence must not be characterised as having committed it.

conviction_record.description: The evidentiary spine of the record. Populate this before any behavioural analysis.

convictions.description: Array of {charge, jurisdiction, date, disposition}. Tier 1 sources strongly preferred.

confirmed_victim_count.description: Count established by conviction or by official investigative confirmation. Not the press figure.

attributed_victim_count.description: Count formally attributed by an investigating agency, including uncharged cases. Must cite the agency.

claimed_victim_count.description: Figure claimed by the offender. Offender self-report is unreliable by default; record it as a datum about the offender, never as a victim count.

estimate_provenance.description: Who produced any higher estimate and on what basis. Estimates with no traceable methodology are excluded from this dataset.

background.description: Biographical antecedents. Childhood accounts in this literature rest heavily on retrospective offender self-report given after arrest; treat accordingly and prefer contemporaneous records.

documented_head_injury.description: Medical documentation only. Self-report is not documentation.

macdonald_triad.description: HISTORICAL CONSTRUCT, NOT A PREDICTOR. Recorded because the older literature uses it and researchers need it for replication studies. Parfitt & Alleyne (2020) found no support for the triad as a predictor of later violence. Do not present these fields as risk indicators.

clinical.description: Formal assessments only. A diagnosis must be attributable to a named clinician who examined the subject, in a citable document. Diagnoses asserted by journalists, documentarians or commentators are excluded — record those under 'commentary_attributions' instead.

psychometric_results.description: Include the instrument used, the administering clinician and the date. A bare IQ number with no instrument is not admissible.

commentary_attributions.description: Diagnostic labels applied in the secondary literature by people who never examined the subject. Recorded as claims about the discourse, not about the person.

offence_behaviour.description: Behavioural coding. Keep to what the evidentiary record supports. Do not reconstruct interior experience the record cannot establish.

victim_selection.description: Structural description of targeting patterns. Describe the access conditions the offender exploited, not the victims' characteristics as if explanatory.

spatial_pattern.description: Marauder / commuter classification per Canter & Larkin (1993). Cite the coding basis.

detection_delay_factors.description: Structural reasons for delayed identification: jurisdictional fragmentation, records systems, victim-class neglect, absent forensic capability.

forensic_methods_used.description: Record the method AND its current scientific standing. Several techniques used in historical convictions (bite-mark comparison, microscopic hair comparison, arson 'indicators') have since been discredited. Flag these with 'method_now_disputed'.

method_now_disputed.description: Set where a conviction rested wholly or partly on a technique later found unreliable. Cite the body that made the finding (NAS 2009, PCAST 2016, Texas Forensic Science Commission, etc.).

confession_reliability.description: Confessions in this literature are frequently inflated, coerced, or traded for procedural advantage. State the circumstances under which any confession was obtained.

known_gaps.description: Explicit list of what this record does not establish. A complete record states its own limits.

excluded_material.description: Widely circulated claims deliberately NOT included, and why. This is how the record resists contamination from dramatisation.
